options: A list of suppliers eligible for electronic payment
A type of business classification
A predefined template of distribution lines that Payables uses to automatically create an invoice's distributions
A report showing all invoices on hold
questions.explain: A distribution set is a reusable template, selected once on an invoice, that generates its distributions automatically.

questions.q: What must be true of the percentages on a Full distribution set?
options: They can total any amount
They are always left at zero
They only apply to Freight lines
They must total exactly 100%
questions.explain: A Full distribution set's percentages across all its lines must add up to exactly 100%.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Skeleton distribution set from a Full distribution set?
options: A Skeleton set fixes the accounts but leaves amounts at zero for entry at invoice time, while a Full set fixes both accounts and percentages
A Skeleton set has no accounts defined at all
A Skeleton set can only be used on credit memos
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: Skeleton sets predefine accounts only; Full sets predefine both accounts and a fixed percentage split.

questions.q: When would a Skeleton distribution set be the better choice over a Full set?
options: When the split between accounts is always identical every time
When the accounts that should be used are always the same, but the actual split varies invoice to invoice
When the invoice has only one line
When the supplier is international
questions.explain: A Skeleton set is useful when the correct accounts are stable but the proportional split legitimately changes each time.

questions.q: Brightfield applies a Full distribution set of 70%/30% to a $10,000 rent invoice. What distributions result?
options: One distribution for the full $10,000
Ten distributions of $1,000 each
No distributions until AP manually enters amounts
A $7,000 distribution and a $3,000 distribution, created automatically
questions.explain: A Full set automatically creates distributions matching its fixed percentage split against the invoice total.
